Title: Israel army chief vows to demilitarise Gaza despite ceasefire
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel's army chief on Tuesday vowed to push on with demilitarising Gaza and disarming Hamas, despite efforts by the United States to advance the ceasefire in the Palestinian territory.
The comments, made during a visit by Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir to the Gaza Strip, follow intermittent Israeli strikes there in recent days, which the military says were targeting militants.
"In Gaza, we are not giving up on the overarching objective – demilitarising the Gaza Strip and disarming Hamas, using all necessary means," Zamir said, according to a military statement.
The Israeli military has said that it will keep pursuing alleged perpetrators of Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack.
"We continue to act systematically to strike Hamas and its leaders wherever they are, including through ongoing activities to prevent it from rebuilding," he added.
"The pursuit of the terrorists who participated in the October 7 massacre continues – everyone who took part in the massacre will live on the run until they are eliminated," Zamir said, calling it a "long-term mission to which... the entire IDF are committed."
Despite a US-backed ceasefire which came into effect in October 2025, bloodshed has continued in the war-shattered territory.
On Monday, Gazan authorities said at least five people were killed by Israeli fire, including two children.
"There will be no containment of threats. We will not allow the enemy to rebuild itself, we will not allow terrorist infrastructure to become entrenched, and we will act at every opportunity to eliminate threats while they are still taking shape," Zamir was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
The United States has sought to advance the fragile Gaza ceasefire plan in recent weeks.
Hamas has endorsed a roadmap published by President Donald Trump's "Board of Peace" under which the militant group would hand over its weapons to a nascent Palestinian technocratic committee.
But Israel has refused to start withdrawing its forces until Palestinian Islamist movement Hamas is fully disarmed.
According to Israeli media reports, the Israeli army has curbed its operations in the Gaza Strip in recent days under US pressure, and has only been carrying out strikes to remove imminent threats to its troops, or to eliminate those who participated in the Oct 7, 2023 attack.
The devastating war in Gaza was triggered by Hamas's attack on Israel, which resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures. Militants also took 251 hostages to Gaza.
Israel responded with a massive offensive in Gaza that has killed at least 73,431 people, according to the Palestinian territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

Title: Brazil fines TikTok $30 mn in 'powerful signal' over child safety
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazil's data protection agency on Tuesday fined TikTok nearly $30 million for failing to implement child safety measures in what it said was a "powerful signal" to social media companies.
Brazil has taken a tough stance on the regulation of social media platforms, cracking down on disinformation and requiring users under 16 to have their accounts linked to those of their parents.
Fabricio Lopes, an enforcement director with the ANPD data protection agency, told a press conference that TikTok "was not taking the necessary measures to prevent adolescents from accessing the platform and from having the data of these children and adolescents processed."
This data was "being used to offer advertising to adolescents."
He said the fine of 153.7 million reais ($29.9 million) was a "powerful signal to other platforms regarding how seriously the ANPD takes this work" and that the agency hoped they "get the message."
TikTok agreed last week to pay $400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Department of Justice over claims that the video-sharing platform collected children's personal data without parental permission.
TOUGHER ENFORCEMENT
The ANPD this month also ordered popular streaming platform Discord to suspend livestreams and video calls after a teenage girl was allegedly encouraged to take her own life during a broadcast.
The agency told AFP that an appeal filed by Discord on Monday against the suspension is under review.
ANPD director Lorena Giuberti Coutinho said the agency had last week initiated proceedings to verify the compliance of 22 social media networks and platforms with a law passed this year to protect children and teens online.
"I think we can expect much stronger enforcement action" in coming months, she said.
In addition to the fine, the ANPD ordered TikTok parent company ByteDance to delete data collected in violation of regulations.
Coutinho said TikTok had committed to suspend all adverts for users who are not logged in.
TikTok has committed to "implementing a compliance plan to improve the protection of children and adolescents," the ANPD said.
The platform will be required to automatically apply stricter privacy settings to accounts belonging to children under the age of 16, strengthen parental supervision systems, and implement stricter content filters.
TikTok did not immediately respond to requests for comment from AFP.
In 2024, the platform X was blocked for 40 days in Brazil, until the social media network owned by the world's richest person, Elon Musk, complied with the Supreme Court's orders to remove accounts spreading disinformation.

Title: Scam prevention must evolve as syndicates exploit psychology, AI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Malaysia needs to rethink its approach to fighting investment scams as syndicates increasingly rely on sophisticated psychological manipulation rather than simple deception.
Senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy said the sharp rise in cases and losses showed conventional awareness campaigns were no longer sufficient.
He told the
New Straits Times
that many victims  knew scams existed but failed to recognise it when they themselves were being manipulated.
"The problem is not simply a lack of knowledge; it is the growing sophistication of criminal persuasion," he said.
"Scammers exploit trust, greed, fear, urgency and the desire for financial security. They increasingly use professional-looking platforms, fake testimonials, fabricated investment records and seemingly legitimate advisers."
Sundramoorthy said this amounted to social engineering, where criminals manipulated victims' decision-making rather than merely deceiving them about an investment product.
He said prevention campaigns should move beyond basic warnings against high returns and instead teach people to recognise manipulation, verify identities and understand how scammers gradually build trust.
"Prevention must become behavioural and intervention-based, rather than simply informational."
Sundramoorthy said the prevalence of victims aged between 31 and 50, particularly private sector employees, dispelled the perception that scam victims were predominantly elderly or financially unsophisticated.
"These are economically active adults who may have regular incomes, savings, access to digital banking and considerable exposure to investment opportunities.
"This demonstrates that vulnerability to scams is not determined primarily by age, education or technological literacy. It is situational and psychological."
He said financially stable individuals could also be attractive targets because they potentially had greater access to savings, credit and borrowing facilities.
"The modern scam victim should therefore not be viewed as 'gullible'. Victimisation can occur when sophisticated criminal persuasion meets ordinary human cognitive biases," he said.
Sundramoorthy said scammers typically combined "fear of missing out", grooming and promises of exceptional returns to progressively manipulate victims.
"Once victims make an initial payment, they become psychologically invested, while fictitious profits displayed on fraudulent platforms reinforce their confidence.
"When they attempt to withdraw their supposed profits, scammers demand further payments for purported taxes, administrative charges or verification requirements," he said, adding that this could trap victims in a cycle of sending more money in the hope of recovering what had already been invested.
Sundramoorthy also warned that artificial intelligence could make investment scams significantly more convincing and easier to conduct at scale.
"The danger is not simply that AI makes scams more convincing. It can make them scalable."
He said combating investment scams required shared responsibility among enforcement agencies, banks, telecommunications companies, social media companies and messaging platforms.
Banks, he said, should be empowered to introduce safeguards such as warnings, cooling-off periods and additional verification when transactions displayed clear scam indicators.
"The objective should be to create multiple intervention points. If one institution fails to detect the scam, another should still have an opportunity to stop the money."
Sundramoorthy said enforcement must also shift from merely arresting money mules towards dismantling the financial infrastructure underpinning organised fraud.
"Ultimately, investment scams should be understood as organised economic crime rather than simply individual acts of deception.
"The real challenge is to disrupt the entire chain including recruitment, grooming, advertising, digital platforms, payment systems, mule accounts and international transfers.
"Unless prevention and enforcement target that ecosystem, criminals will continue to replace arrested individuals with new recruits, while the number of victims and financial losses continue to grow."

Title: 'US set to revoke visas of up to 200,000 foreigners'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
PRESIDENT Donald Trump's administration is preparing to revoke business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are seeking asylum status in the United States, the Associated Press (AP) reported on Monday.
The report cited State Department documents obtained by AP and two US officials.
If the move is implemented, it would be the largest single mass revocation of visas in US history, according to AP.
The State Department was expected to announce in the coming weeks the revocation of B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders had sought asylum or are now seeking asylum, said the report, adding that the action would be coordinated with the Homeland Security Department.
The B1 and B2 visas are issued for business and tourism ​travel.
The visa revocations would not necessarily result in immediate deportation, said the AP report, citing officials.
Most of those with asylum cases currently pending would be recategorised but would lose their status as business or tourism travellers, the report added.
On Monday, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau alleged on X that the American immigration system "has long been swamped by frivolous asylum claims".
The State Department said earlier this month it had revoked more than 175,000 visas from foreign nationals under the Trump administration.
Trump has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown that he said was aimed at improving domestic security.
Rights groups said the crackdown had violated free speech and due process rights and created an unsafe environment particularly for ethnic minorities. — REUTERS

Title: Social media and FOMO fuel investment scams [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Investment scam syndicates are increasingly exploiting social media, online relationships and victims' "fear of missing out" to lure Malaysians into fraudulent schemes.
Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said scammers were no longer reliant on telephone calls and fake websites alone.
Instead, syndicates use multiple digital platforms to identify potential victims and draw them into fraudulent investments.
He said Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and other social media platforms were commonly used to identify targets before conversations shifted to WhatsApp, Telegram and other messaging applications.
Victims could then be placed in groups purportedly run by "investment experts", "financial mentors" or "professional traders".
Rusdi said syndicates promoted purported investments ranging from Ponzi schemes to cryptocurrency and gold.
Another tactic involved so-called love scams, where victims were "cultivated"  through online relationships before being persuaded to invest in non-existent schemes.
"Investment scam syndicates continuously evolve alongside developments in digital technology and changes in how people use social media," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Rusdi said "fear of missing out", or FOMO, was another factor exploited by scammers, with victims sometimes rushing into financial decisions for fear of missing an apparently lucrative opportunity.
Police said Malaysians lost RM413.81 million in 4,279 investment scam cases between January and June — an average of RM96,700 per case, or RM2.29 million a day.
The daily figure is equivalent to over 27 years of gross income for a household earning the national median of RM7,017 a month.
Theoretically, RM2.29 million could pay for between 54 and 65 People's Housing Programme (PPR) units, based on government selling prices of RM35,000 to RM42,000 each.
Police statistics show investment scams are not confined to retirees or people with limited financial knowledge, with victims cutting across age groups and occupations.
People aged between 31 and 50 formed the largest group of victims, followed by those aged 21 to 30 and 51 to 60.
Private sector employees were the most commonly affected group, followed by civil servants, the self-employed and retirees.
Rusdi said the figures showed investment scams also affected professionals and those earning steady incomes.
RACE TO STOP STOLEN FUNDS
The movement of stolen savings also remains a major challenge for investigators.
Investigations showed that some mule accounts belonged to people who sold, rented or lent their bank accounts to syndicates for payment, while others involved those tricked into opening accounts for third parties.
Police have also urged victims to report suspected scams immediately, as stolen funds can move through mule accounts within a short period before being withdrawn or transferred overseas.
Rusdi said the existing account-freezing mechanism involving the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC), CCID, Bank Negara Malaysia and financial institutions remained an important tool in disrupting scam transactions.
NSRC statistics showed that RM34.05 million was earmarked and RM17.49 million frozen last year.
Between January and June this year, RM5.58 million was earmarked while RM7.29 million was frozen. In 2024, RM26.13 million was earmarked and RM7.01 million frozen.
Rusdi said the earlier a report was lodged with the NSRC and police, the greater the chance of earmarking and freezing funds before they were moved elsewhere.
He also said Malaysians should make it a habit to verify investment opportunities before committing their savings.
"There is no investment that can guarantee high returns within a short period without risk."
The threat is expected to become more sophisticated as syndicates exploit advances in technology.
Rusdi said artificial intelligence and deepfake technology were becoming major challenges, allowing scammers to create increasingly convincing audio, video and visual content to impersonate legitimate people and companies.
He said police wanted greater use of real-time data sharing, automated detection of suspicious transactions and AI-based data analytics to strengthen the response to scams.
The CCID is working with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, CyberSecurity Malaysia, Securities Commission Malaysia and other agencies to strengthen early detection of platforms and content suspected of being used for scams.
Rusdi said fighting investment scams required more than enforcement and awareness campaigns, with cooperation between government agencies, financial institutions, technology platforms and the public becoming increasingly important.
"An offer that is too good to be true is usually an early indication of a scam."

Title: Two retirees lose RM750,000 after falling for investment scams
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  She lost  more than RM500,000 of her retirement savings to an investment scam. Amira (not her real name) is now struggling to pick up the pieces and hopes her ordeal will warn others against making the same mistake.
The 69-year-old woman urges others, particularly those investing their savings, not to be swayed by promises of attractive returns.
What began as an opportunity to grow her retirement funds eventually cost her a substantial portion of savings built up over more than three decades.
"I hope people will be more careful and learn from what happened to me.
"Don't simply trust people when it comes to investments. Check everything properly and don't make the same mistakes I did," she said.
Amira worked for a private company for 34 years and had never touched her Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings.
After  retiring several years ago, she withdrew nearly RM900,000 from her EPF account and deposited it in a bank.
She was introduced by an agent to several investment schemes promising lucrative returns.
Amira did not realise  that she was being drawn into schemes that would eventually leave her more than RM500,000  poorer.
"I did not invest the sum in one go. I don't remember the exact amount, but I made many transactions which snowballed," she said.
Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department  director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said syndicates were increasingly using sophisticated methods to make bogus schemes appear legitimate, including impersonating genuine investment companies as well as using names, logos, websites, documents and testimonials to gain victims' confidence.
He added that investment scams continued to thrive because of advances in digital technology, allowing syndicate tactics and psychological manipulation to evolve.
The loss has been particularly painful for Amira as the money was meant to sustain her through retirement and help care for her 90-year-old mother, a stroke patient.
Looking back, Amira said her experience showed how easily people could be persuaded to part with money when an investment appeared convincing and profitable.
"If something seems too good to be true, don't trust it. It's better to choose a safer option than lose your entire life savings," she stressed.
She hopes her story will help others recognise warning signs, carry out proper checks and resist the pressure to invest more simply because they have committed to it.
Another retiree, identified only as Noor, 65, said she lost RM250,000 after investing her retirement savings in a bogus scheme.
The former senior manager at a semi-government organisation said the money came from her EPF savings accumulated throughout her career.
She had opted for early retirement in 2019 to care for her ailing mother.
Noor said she was introduced to the investment scheme by an agent she had known for years and who had previously handled her unit trust investments.
"I trusted the person because I had known the agent for a long time. I thought my retirement savings could generate an income once I stopped working.
"For the first four months, I received RM8,000 in returns before the company stopped paying monthly dividends and said it wanted to 'return' my RM250,000 capital early.
"But until today, there has been no news.
"Now, I have to sell whatever assets I have just to survive. If God gives me another 10 or 15 years, I don't even know whether the money I have left will be enough," she said.
Rusdi said syndicates could make bogus investments appear genuine by showing purported profits and providing fake investment applications or platforms that gave victims the impression their money was generating real returns.
Fake testimonials and claims that other investors were making profits could further build confidence before victims are persuaded to invest more.
Both women said the experience had made them more cautious and urged retirees and those approaching retirement not to be swayed by investments promising unusually high returns within a short period.
Amira and Noor's experiences underscore the wider scale of investment scams, which have cost Malaysians hundreds of millions of ringgit.
Last year, police recorded 9,603 cases involving RM1.466 billion in losses, compared with 6,337 cases involving RM848.63 million in 2024.
A total of 2,059 people were arrested in connection with investment scams during the six-month period, while 1,460 were charged.

Title: Terengganu Perhilitan moves rescued elephant to Perak
Article:

TERENGGANU Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has relocated a female elephant that was found roaming around Kampung Jeram, Manir, last Friday.
Its director, Dennis Ten, said the elephant was rescued on Saturday.
The relocation began at 8am yesterday and involved 13  members from Terengganu Perhilitan, seven from Sungai Deka Elephant Conservation Centre and two from the National Elephant Conservation Centre in Kuala Gandah, Pahang.
"The wild elephant was in a safe and stable condition throughout the relocation process. It was transported to Royal Belum State Park in Perak for release."
Ten also expressed his appreciation to all agencies involved in the elephant's relocation for their support and cooperation.

Title: Trump threatens to rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was considering renaming Lake Ontario as "Lake America" as his trade war with Canada escalated.
The threat – which Trump backed up with a map featuring the new name – mirrored his move to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America last year.
Trump stepped up his rhetoric as Canada announced a volley of tit-for-tat tariffs on US goods after trade talks between the historically close allies broke down on Friday.
"The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don't expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer," Trump said on his Truth Social network.
Lake Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes located on the border between Canada and the United States.
It shares a name with the Canadian province of Ontario, which borders the lake along with the US state of New York. Toronto, Canada's largest city, sits on the northwestern shore of the lake.
Trump later posted a map with the words "Lake Ontario" crossed out and replaced with "Lake America" in large gold font with a US flag, which was boosted by pro-Trump social media accounts.
The lake threat comes as Trump reups his push for Canada to become the 51st US state and the trade war between the two countries escalates.
But it also reflects a peculiarly personal spat with Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who said Monday that the US president could "kiss my ass" and threatened a surcharge on exported electricity.
During his second presidency, Trump has irked a series of allies with his outlandish territorial claims.
Mexico has refused to accept his executive order renaming of the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America on his first day back in office on January 20.

Title: Penang schools to halt outdoor activities if API reading tops 100
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
PENANG schools have been ordered to halt outdoor activities if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100 as part of the state's haze preparedness measures.
The state Education Department said schools must also close immediately once the API reading exceeded 200, in line with existing guidelines.
Up to 9pm on Monday, Penang was among 28 locations recording unhealthy API levels.
"We are monitoring the haze conditions and API readings across Penang, with the safety, health and well-being of students and education personnel remaining our top priority," it told the "New Straits Times".
The department said schools and district education offices had been directed to monitor official readings from the Department of Environment.
"Schools must ensure students drink enough water and minimise their exposure to outdoor air.
"Particular attention should be given to those with health problems. Such students should be referred to nearby health facilities, with their parents or guardians informed."
The department also encouraged students and school staff to wear face masks as a precaution.
It has instructed schools to maintain open communication with parents and guardians to ensure any changes to school operations or haze-related directives are communicated promptly.
"Schools must report measures taken to their respective district education offices and the state Education Department to facilitate monitoring and coordination."
An API reading of zero to 50 is "good", 51 to 100 is "moderate", 101 to 200 is "unhealthy", 201 to 300 is "very unhealthy" and above 300 is considered "hazardous".

Title: Miti to implement low-altitude economy  project
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry will implement the Unmanned Valley Ecosystem pilot project to drive the development of the low-altitude economy (LAE).
LAE refers to economic activities and public services conducted within a low-altitude airspace ecosystem using technologies such as drones, advanced air mobility, air logistics, infrastructure inspection, smart farming and emergency services.
The sector also includes unmanned aerial vehicles, air taxis, and vertical take-off and landing electric aircraft.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the project would be carried out under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), with the proposed pilot project to be located at universities.
"The government under the National Aerospace Industry Corporation of Malaysia is planning to establish an 'unmanned valley', where all flights, including the vertiport system, can be tested.
"Rolling out the pilot project at universities will attract the younger generation because, ultimately, they will be the ones to use this technology," he told Bernama after appearing on Bernama TV's Ruang Bicara programme titled "Low-Altitude Economic Development, Digitalisation & Aerospace" on Monday.
Sim, however, said that they are also open to suggestions for other suitable locations to implement the pilot project.
He said the pilot project's implementation must take into account several challenges, especially regarding safety, to ensure the technology can be tested and developed properly.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke previously said the LAE guidelines are expected to be announced by the end of this year, providing a regulatory, operational and governance framework to ensure safe airspace integration in the sector.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia is developing the guidelines, which are expected to be announced at the Asian Transport Expo 2026. — BERNAMA

Title: TH RCI: MCW questions why former auditor general not called to testify
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Corruption Watch (MCW) has questioned whether all evidence relating to the Tabung Haji (TH) issue was fairly tested before conclusions were reached by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), particularly given that former Auditor-General Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad was not called to testify.
MCW said the RCI report showed that Madinah had submitted a statutory declaration as a witness but was not called to give evidence before the commission.
This was despite the RCI subsequently making critical assessments of the actions of the then Auditor-General, it said.
"MCW's question is not who we should blindly believe, but whether all evidence was fairly tested before conclusions were reached.
"In fighting corruption, we must have the courage to pursue the truth, even when it does not support any political narrative. Corruption must be proven, mismanagement must be held accountable and audits must be open to scrutiny. But slogans cannot replace evidence," it said in a statement today.
The statement follows a report by Berita Harian that Madinah said the RCI's findings on TH might have been different had she been called to testify as the former Auditor-General.
Madinah said the 2017 Auditor-General's Report, prepared by her and her team, did not identify evidence of direct theft at TH.
She had said she would be the first to lodge a report with the authorities if direct theft at the institution during the period examined by the RCI was proven.
MCW said Madinah's explanation had introduced an aspect that warranted closer examination in the debate over TH.
It said the issue was no longer simply about determining who was right or wrong, but about distinguishing between audit findings, professional judgment, governance failures and allegations of misconduct.
"An audit by the National Audit Department recorded TH's 2017 profit at about RM3.4 billion. A Financial Position Review by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), after adjustments of nearly RM4.8 billion, resulted in an adjusted loss of about RM1.4 billion.
"However, the two reviews had different mandates, scopes and approaches. Impairment does not necessarily mean embezzlement.
"Asset impairment is an accounting issue. It may point to poor investment decisions, weaknesses in risk management or disputed accounting policies.
"But to claim that money was embezzled, we need evidence of who took it, how it was taken and where it went.
"At the same time, this argument cannot be used to dismiss the RCI's serious findings. The RCI questioned TH's impairment policy, asset-liability position, hibah payments and the National Audit Department's audit decisions. All these issues must be addressed substantively," it said.
The RCI report, published on July 29, found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in the 2017 financial year, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported in its financial statements.
The report said that if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied for 2017, TH would have recorded the net loss, indicating that its financial position was already critical that year.

Title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on US$20 billion worth of US goods
Article:
OTTAWA: Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion (US$19.94 billion) worth of United States goods, matching dollar-for-dollar new duties imposed by Washington, and unveiled financial support for Canadian businesses and workers caught in the escalating trade war.
The counter-tariffs take effect on US goods from Sept 8 and will impose duties of 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent across 700 products imported from south of the border, a government statement said.
In terms of financial support for affected workers and industries, Canada announced a C$7.5 billion package of new and enhanced measures including support for small and medium-sized businesses, a stream for funding cash flows of companies, and support for workers who could be at risk due to the new tariffs.
From Saturday, President Donald Trump's new 50 per cent tariffs across US$20 billion of Canadian imports took effect after talks between the two countries to avert the tariffs collapsed. The new tit-for-tat tariffs mark a new low in the Canada-US relationship.
"Our dollar-for-dollar, rate for rate counter-tariffs as well as a multi-billion dollar support package will protect workers, farmers, families, and businesses," Canada's Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said.
The new tariffs are designed so that the impact on Canadian consumers and businesses is minimal and could still hit the US, a government official said.
The 50 per cent tariffs are on some important sectors such as steel, aluminium, furniture and clothing, 25 per cent tariffs are on cheese, appliances and some seafood, while the 15 per cent tariffs will be on electronics and tools, the official said. — REUTERS

Title: Ramkarpal urges govt to expedite Sosma amendments
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Bukit Gelugor member of parliament Ramkarpal Singh has urged the government to announce when amendments to Sosma will be tabled, saying the delay requires urgent attention.
Ramkarpal, who is DAP national legal bureau chairman, said he took note of former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay's defence of the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma).
Ayob had said specialised laws were necessary to deal effectively with terrorism and organised crime.
Ramkarpal, however, maintained that Sosma was draconian, arguing that it removed judicial oversight over the detention of suspects for up to 28 days and further restricted bail in most cases.
He also raised concerns over the use of Sosma against ordinary citizens and those allegedly involved in gang-related activities, saying there had been instances where the law was abused.
"Furthermore, it is apparent that Sosma seems to be used on ordinary citizens or those involved in gang-related activities, and there have been instances where its use has been abused in the past," he said in a statement today.
Ramkarpal cited the detention of a 16-year-old girl in Kedah under Sosma as an example.
He said he had raised the possibility of abolishing or, at the very least, amending Sosma in Parliament in January.
He said the call was also supported by Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man at the time.
He added that Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had indicated that a Bill to amend Sosma was expected to be tabled at the next Parliament meeting.
"However, there have not been any developments on this since," he added.
Ramkarpal said the government should provide clarity on the status of the proposed amendments, given the time that had elapsed.
"In the circumstances, I call on the government to announce when the said amendments will be tabled as the matter has been delayed for too long and requires urgent attention," he said.

Title: Don't repeat RCI just because findings don't suit, says PKR Youth chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was established to seek the truth based on facts and evidence, not to yield decisions in favour of any political party, says PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim.
He questioned the rationale behind demands by Perikatan Nasional and Umno for a new RCI to re-investigate the management of the institution.
He said the RCI report, made public last month, was not initiated by the Madani Government, adding that the setup process began when the parties now demanding a new probe were in administration.
"When the RCI findings do not favour their political narrative, suddenly they want a new RCI. What exactly do they want?
"Should a new RCI be established every time an investigation's findings do not meet their political expectations, until a decision they like is reached?" he said in a statement today.
Kamil said if there were errors in the RCI report, the parties concerned should present evidence instead of rejecting the findings simply because they did not align with their political interests.
"If there is truly new evidence, present it. If there are factual discrepancies, show them. If there were errors in the investigation process, explain them openly. That is how a mature democracy works, not by asking for an RCI to be repeated simply because they are dissatisfied with its findings," he said.
He also raised the issue of PN members of parliament who chose to walk out when the RCI report was tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Aug 12, despite having been given space to listen to and scrutinise the investigation findings.
"Today, when the RCI findings are not in their favour, they demand that a new RCI be set up. This raises a major question as to whether they truly want to seek the truth, or merely want a decision that suits their political narrative," he said.
He also reminded all parties not to make TH a political tool to serve specific interests, as the institution held the trust of millions of depositors.
He said the Madani Government was not afraid of the truth, and if there were any shortcomings or legal violations, appropriate action must be taken.
"I call on PN and Umno to stop playing games with state institutions for political gain. If they genuinely want to defend TH, defend it with solid facts, evidence, and arguments," he said.
The RCI report published on July 29 revealed various key findings regarding TH's management and governance for the period between 2014 and 2020.

Title: Celebrity preacher, NGO secretary to face RM12.3mil misappropriation charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will charge the chairman of a non-governmental organisation (NGO), who is also a celebrity preacher, and the NGO's secretary at the Seremban Sessions Court tomorrow over the alleged misappropriation of more than RM12 million.
According to a press invitation issued by the agency today, the celebrity preacher and the NGO secretary, both in their 30s, will be charged at 9am.
On April 22, the Negri Sembilan MACC was reported to have arrested a freelance preacher suspected of abusing his position and misappropriating about RM12.3 million in NGO funds for personal gain.
Following the investigation, the Negri Sembilan MACC froze 15 accounts comprising three personal accounts, three NGO accounts and nine company accounts, with a total value of about RM16.5 million.
The MACC also seized RM6,576 in cash, as well as foreign currency comprising SAR95,568 and SGD795.
Also seized were three watches worth about RM5,000, three handbags (RM3,000), five bracelets (RM26,000), a ring (RM2,000), a necklace (RM7,000) and 51 one-gramme gold pieces worth about RM31,000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drafting of new E-Commerce Act must be expedited, says Fuziah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The drafting of a new E-Commerce Act must be expedited to strengthen consumer protection and ensure micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and local traders can compete fairly in an increasingly complex digital ecosystem.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the move was crucial to address gaps in the Electronic Commerce Act 2006, particularly in consumer protection and cross-border transactions.
She said the country's e-commerce framework must keep pace with technological advancements and changing consumer and business practices.
"We need to protect MSMEs and local traders. While competitive pricing benefits consumers, we must avoid unbalanced competition that could cause local traders to lose their market share and livelihoods in the future," she said in a Facebook post today.
Fuziah said foreign sellers conducting business with consumers in Malaysia must also comply with clear standards of responsibility and regulatory requirements to protect consumers from fraud, unsafe products and disputes.
She said the responsibilities of e-commerce platforms also need to be clearly defined, as modern platforms are no longer merely venues connecting sellers and buyers but increasingly influence how products are marketed, sold and delivered to consumers.
Fuziah also said foreign participation in the e-commerce sector must generate added value for Malaysia through investments, job opportunities, talent development and technology transfer, while creating greater opportunities for local enterprises within the supply chain.
"We want trade and foreign participation to genuinely add value to Malaysia, bringing in investments, jobs, talent development and technology transfer, while opening up more space for local enterprises in the supply chain.
"It is not just about low prices; it is about creating a healthier ecosystem where MSMEs and local traders have room to grow and compete on a level playing field," she said.
Last Thursday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the government would expedite the drafting of an e-commerce bill to improve facilitation and regulation in the sector in line with the rapid growth of digital business.
Anwar said the measure was crucial to ensuring the orderly development of the e-commerce ecosystem while providing support and protection for all stakeholders, including young people and new entrepreneurs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From Tokyo to London, heatwaves send men to work in shorts
Article:
SCORCHING  summer temperatures have done what decades of dress-down Fridays have failed to do — get men to the office in shorts.
Japan's capital led the way. This year the metropolitan government's long-standing no-tie, no-jacket "Cool Biz" campaign took a step further by encouraging its staff to ditch long trousers, and even try T-shirts and sneakers.
As heatwaves mounted across Europe, other workers followed in Tokyo's wake, sometimes with the encouragement of authorities and management, sometimes without.
Major retailers said linen shorts and suits were flying off the shelves in Britain, as men opted for breathable fabrics more commonly associated with Mediterranean climes.
"The lines between 'commuter' and 'holiday' style are blurring," said Martha Hibberd, menswear buyer at British department store John Lewis.
Marks and Spencer said sales of men's linen trousers in June to July jumped 183 per cent compared with the same period a year ago.
H&M — one of Europe's biggest fashion retailers — said it was bringing in lighter clothes and delaying the release of autumnal lines to later in the year.
"It looks like we're not going back when it comes to climate change," said Andreas Lowenstam, H&M's head of menswear design.
Hugo Boss said it has increased its assortment of tailored shorts. Its "Boss by Beckham" range in collaboration with football star David Beckham offers a pair of cotton tailored shorts for €229.
The trend was there to see in Europe's business hubs, from London's Canary Wharf to the streets of Frankfurt. But there were some limits.
At Norway's largest bank, DNB, staff were welcome to wear shorts and skirts, said spokesperson Vidar Korsberg Dalsbo.
"However, we are probably talking about smarter garments with some length rather than a ballerina skirt or a cheeky pair of 1970s-style football shorts."
In June, Gianfranco Lot, Switzerland head at insurance group Swiss Re, wrote an email to staff with tips on how to stay cool.
Alongside the list of suggestions — such as drinking water, breaking when needed, and taking a dip in Lake Zurich just across from the office — there was a quick reminder that "shorts are for weekends".
Pushing back against the traditions, there were signs that some workers were prepared to take a stand for their lighter attire.
Germany's biggest union, IG Metall, and services sector union Verdi both said they believed that dress codes should be relaxed or waived if necessary at times of higher temperatures.
"Summers are getting hotter, heatwaves are becoming more frequent, and the strain on workers is noticeably increasing," said Moriz Tiedemann, occupational health expert at IG Metall.
Some were already taking matters into their own hands.
In Warsaw, one bus driver decided he had had enough of the standard uniform of long polyester trousers and turned up to work one day this month in a skirt, as a protest.
"These materials make us sweat and overheat," said the man, who only gave his name as Darek.
At the last count, a petition launched by one of his colleagues, asking the Polish capital's transport authority ZTM to let drivers wear shorts during hot weather, had collected more than 400 signatures.
The writers are from Reuters

Title: Azmin rules out PKR return, vows to stay with Bersatu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, who is now with Bersatu, will not return to his former party despite an open invitation to past members.
Azmin, who is also Bersatu secretary-general, said he remains confident that his current party serves as the right platform for his political future.
Although Bersatu faces challenges, the Hulu Kelang assemblyman signalled that the party's time will come.
"Bersatu's time will come. Continue working sincerely.
"Bersatu remains the platform of my struggle. I will not be discouraged by a single setback. Tomorrow is another day," he told Berita Harian.
PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when delivering his presidential address at the PKR Annual Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) recently, urged former party leaders and activists to return to PKR.
Previously, it was reported that former Bandar Tun Razak member of parliament Kamarudin Jaffar and former Nibong Tebal member of parliament Mansor Othman were expected to rejoin PKR.
Former PKR vice-president Datuk Dr Xavier Jayakumar also confirmed he had rejoined the party.
On Feb 24, 2020, Azmin was sacked from PKR.
The decision regarding his dismissal was announced by PKR secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail following a Central Leadership Council (MPP) meeting.

Title: Crude volume debate masks real shortage of refined fuels
Article:
THE crude oil market is currently engaged in the wrong debate over how much oil is actually moving via the Strait of Hormuz. It should be debating the constrained flows of refined products around Asia.
United States Energy Secretary Chris Wright has repeatedly claimed that much more crude is getting through the disputed strait than vessel-tracking analysts such as Kpler can see.
One of Wright's claims was that about 15 million barrels per day (bpd) exited the Strait of Hormuz on a day last week, which if true would take volumes close to what they were before the US and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28.
Wright has also said transits averaged about nine million bpd over a seven-day period, although he didn't specify the exact dates and he has not provided details such as vessel names and their intended destinations.
Vessel monitoring services estimate that around five million bpd is leaving Hormuz, and that includes so-called dark transits and ship-to-ship transfers from smaller vessels to larger tankers in the Gulf of Oman.
But the dispute over crude oil volumes is a false debate. If Wright is correct then Asia's oil imports will start to pick up in coming weeks as the crude he claims is leaving the Middle East arrives at ports.
It's considerably easier to track import volumes, so it's merely a matter of time before the market can assess whether Wright is correct, or whether his numbers are overstated.
In the meantime, Asia's refined products markets remain stressed, as shown by sharply lower volumes and extremely elevated refining margins.
Asia's imports of light and middle distillates for this month are estimated by Kpler at 5.59 million bpd, in line with the 5.60 million bpd seen last month.
However, these volumes are down 21 per cent from the 7.08 million bpd average in the three months to the end of February.
In effect, Asia is having to absorb a drop of 1.49 million bpd of key fuels such as diesel, jet fuel and petrol.
The impact is also not being evenly spread across the world's top-energy consuming continent, with less wealthy countries shouldering a bigger share of the loss of product volumes.
Indonesia's imports of light and middle distillates are estimated at 432,000 bpd in August, the lowest in 13 months and down from an average of 533,000 bpd in the three months prior to the start of the Iran conflict.
The Philippines is expected to see arrivals of 257,000 bpd of light and middle distillates this month, down from an average of 362,000 bpd in the three months to the end of February.
A wealthier country like Australia, the world's biggest importer of diesel, is managing to secure the same levels of fuel, with August imports of light and middle distillates estimated by Kpler at 863,0000 bpd, only slightly below the 880,000 bpd in the three months prior to the war.
But securing fuel is coming at a high cost, with product prices remaining near record high levels and refining margins staying elevated.
The profit of making a barrel of gasoil, the building block for diesel, at a Singapore refinery was US$71.29 a barrel on Aug 21, down from the record high of US$85.63 on March 30 but also 226 per cent higher than the US$21.90 that prevailed on Feb 27, the day before the conflict started.
Most of the stress in refined products has been felt in middle distillates, given the constrained supply of Middle East crudes, many of which are medium in gravity.
Asia's refineries are tailored to process this type of oil into products such as diesel and jet fuel.
But even petrol, the main light distillate, is commanding a high premium, with the profit margin ending at US$20.74 a barrel on Aug 21, up 159 per cent from US$8 on Feb 27.
The message the market is giving is that while there may be sufficient crude oil reaching Asia, it's not necessarily the correct grades and those countries with spare refining capacity aren't ramping up exports to meet demand.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: NST Leader: Rise and rise of haze hotspots
Article:
MALAYSIA has lived through repeated haze crises, particularly the disastrous 2015 episode, and Asean has had more than two decades to build a mechanism to prevent a repeat.
Yet here we are again, with unhealthy air spreading across Peninsular Malaysia and experts warning that the haze could persist until late September.
Serian in Sarawak — one of the six hotspots in the state — has recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 192 in the country. The other five locations in Sarawak are said to be recording among the worst readings.
The 13 locations in Peninsular Malaysia are not doing any better. Thanks to prevailing winds from Kalimantan and Sumatra in Indonesia, transboundary haze has reached Sarawak and several locations in the west coast of the peninsula.
Asean has had a framework since 2002. The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution came into force in 2003 and requires member states to cooperate on prevention, monitoring, mitigation and enforcement.
Indonesia, the source of much of the region's worst haze, finally ratified the agreement in January 2015 — just months before the catastrophic haze that year. The problem is not a lack of agreements. Asean ministers have repeatedly reaffirmed commitments, established monitoring mechanisms and promoted joint firefighting and information sharing.
Like it or not, Indonesia must shoulder the greatest responsibility. The fires are predominantly occurring in Indonesia, particularly in fire-prone areas of Sumatra and Kalimantan. Indonesian authorities themselves acknowledge that fires are frequently associated with land clearing and agriculture. Indonesia's enforcement record deserves tougher scrutiny.
Jakarta has announced firefighting operations, arrests and warnings against open burning.
Those actions are welcome, but the problem is they are not preventive. Malaysia can't do anything about fighting forest and land fires in Indonesia.
What Putrajaya can do is to work with Jakarta to stop the fires. One option is joint cloud-seeding operations. No doubt this is not a preventive measure. Also, it is not the best of the curative methods as experts in many countries have warned. Back to prevention.
Here is a question for the Indonesian authorities: Why are fires repeatedly allowed to become massive peatland and forest fires before decisive action is taken? Indonesia's authorities should be identifying and prosecuting those responsible for fires, including commercial interests where evidence points to them, rather than treating them as a natural disaster.
Good neighbourliness requires more than firefighting after the damage is done. Indonesia cannot expect its neighbours to accept recurring transboundary pollution as an unavoidable consequence of its dry season.
If land clearing, plantation practices and peatland management are contributing to fires, those practices must be regulated and enforced.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man killed, another arrested after group fight in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Police have arrested a man following a group fight at Jalan Mandolin 33/5, Taman Alam Megah, which resulted in the death of another man.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said police were alerted after a member of the public reported a fight involving a group of men.
"Preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred at 2pm. CCTV footage showed several men involved in a confrontation, during which slashing took place
"A car then struck one of the suspects, killing him at the scene," he said in a statement.
Police subsequently arrested a man in connection with the incident.
An investigation paper has been opened under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and at least 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
Those with information can contact investigating officer Assistant Superintendent Shamsiah Noor Zakaria at 012-830 8706, or the nearest police station.
The incident went viral earlier after a dashcam recording from a vehicle near the scene was circulated online.
In the one-minute video, a group of people were seen rushing out of several vehicles before attacking a man lying on the road.
Another car was then seen making a U-turn and hitting an individual before several others attacked him.

Title: Anwar pays tribute to 'Father of MRSM' Abdul Wahab Alwi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended his condolences to the family of Maktab Rendah Sains Mara (MRSM) founder Abdul Wahab Alwi, who died early this morning.
In a Facebook post, Anwar described Abdul Wahab, known as the "Father of MRSM", as having made significant contributions to national education.
"The late Abdul Wahab's contribution to conceptualising and developing the MRSM initiative was a major contribution to the history of education in the country, particularly in expanding access to science education for Malaysian children.
"May Allah SWT shower His mercy upon his soul, forgive his sins, and place him among His righteous servants," Anwar said.
The prime minister said Abdul Wahab's efforts helped MRSM grow into an institution that has produced many Malaysians who are knowledgeable, skilled, and successful across various fields.
Abdul Wahab died at 3am today. He was 84.

Title: Agriculture, logistics set to reap early gains from Malaysia's low-altitude economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Agriculture and logistics are expected to see the most immediate benefits from the development of Malaysia's low-altitude economy (LAE), according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
The LAE refers to economic activities conducted in lower airspace using drones, unmanned aircraft and air taxis for purposes including agriculture, deliveries, infrastructure inspection, surveillance, mapping, disaster response and passenger transport.
CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said drones were already being used in plantations in northern Malaysia for various agricultural activities.
"They can be used for precision fertilising, monitoring crops and other activities. These can be carried out more efficiently, making agriculture one of the major areas," he said on Bernama TV's The Nation programme titled "Understanding the Low-Altitude Economy Framework" today.
Norazman said logistics also offered significant potential, particularly for transporting essential supplies to rural and hard-to-reach communities in Sabah and Sarawak.
"Because of our geographical location, this is another area that is viable for us to explore," he said.
He also identified surveillance and mapping as areas where drones could replace helicopters.
"In Peninsular Malaysia alone, the pipeline network is 1,900 kilometres long. Can you imagine deploying a helicopter to inspect this pipeline?
"We already use drones for this purpose, not across all 1,900 kilometres, of course, but along certain sections in rural areas," he said.
Norazman explained that drones not only conduct surveillance but also collect data for analysis, allowing operators to take a more proactive approach.
"With all the data, you can be more proactive in determining whether you need regular surveillance and how the intervals can be spaced out. This creates efficiency," he said.
Meanwhile, Norazman said that while drones and air taxis were the most visible elements of the LAE, a much larger supporting ecosystem operated behind them.
"Take pilots, for instance. We already have 6 remote-pilot training organisations and 7,000 qualified drone pilots, but that is only one part of the ecosystem, alongside aircraft production and manufacturing.
"Another thing is that when you talk about the LAE, it needs telecommunications. The infrastructure in Malaysia is already present. We have more than 20,000 telecommunications towers that these drones can use," he said.
Norazman said Malaysia was also investing heavily in data centres, as every operation needed to be analysed to ensure future operations were conducted safely.
He added that when the LAE framework was introduced, it would not necessarily consolidate all regulations involving multiple agencies, but would complement them within a single framework.
"This will allow everybody to make use of the low-altitude economy safely so that we are all on the same page," he said.
The LAE framework is expected to be introduced by the end of 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen dies after being struck by lorry following motorcycle fall
Article:
KOTA BELUD: A 16-year-old student was killed after being hit by a lorry after the motorcycle he was riding skidded on Jalan Kota Belud-Kota Marudu near Kampung Jawi-Jawi here this evening.
The victim, Muhammad Safwan Muad, a student of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Taun Gusi, was pronounced dead at the scene.
District police chief Superintendent Khairul Shah Peri said preliminary investigations found that the 46-year-old lorry driver was travelling from Kota Marudu towards Tuaran.
He said the victim was riding a Yamaha Ego motorcycle with a 15-year-old pillion rider from Sembirai towards Kudat.
"Upon reaching the location in rainy conditions, the motorcycle carrying the two teenagers is believed to have skidded.
"After falling, the pillion rider got up and moved towards the left road shoulder, while the rider is believed to have run towards the lorry's path," he said when contacted today.
Khairul Shah said the lorry driver was believed to have been unable to avoid the victim due to the short distance before the collision.
"The victim was pronounced dead at the scene by Kota Belud Hospital medical personnel, while the pillion rider and lorry driver were uninjured.
"An inspection found no damage to the motorcycle, while the lorry's front bumper was dented," he said.
He said it was drizzling after rain at the time, while the road was straight and paved.
The victim's body was taken to the Kota Belud Hospital Forensic Unit for further action.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar man to be charged with sexually assaulting Australian boy
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 30-year-old Myanmar national will be charged at the Sessions Court here tomorrow with sexually assaulting a 3-year-old Australian boy.
Northeast district deputy police chief Superintendent Lee Swee Sake confirmed that the suspect would face a charge under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The incident occurred on Aug 20 while the boy was dining with his parents and younger sibling at a temporary hawker site along New Lane.
The suspect, a worker at one of the food stalls, reportedly approached the child and touched his private parts.
The victim's family caught the suspect in the act and immediately lodged a police report, leading to his arrest at the scene.
During questioning, the suspect admitted to touching the boy, claiming he did so because he thought the child was cute.
The victim and his family, who are from Australia, arrived in Malaysia on Aug 19 for a holiday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three killed in two-car crash in Kota Tingg
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Three people, including a woman, were killed in a collision involving two cars along Jalan Jemaluang here today.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations centre said it received an emergency call about the crash at 5.05pm, prompting the dispatch of teams from the Kota Tinggi and Mersing fire stations.
"Upon arrival, firefighters found the crash involved a Honda City carrying a 21-year-old man and a 20-year-old woman, and a Toyota Vios driven by a 31-year-old man.
"All three victims were confirmed dead at the scene by Health Ministry medical personnel," the department said in a statement.
Firefighters extricated the victims from the wreckage before handing their bodies over to police.
The operation, led by Senior Fire Officer II Azlan Hamzah, was brought under control at 6.45pm and concluded at 6.59pm.
The cause of the accident is under investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firefighters recover woman's body from 8th floor
Article:
BAYAN LEPAS: Firefighters were called in to recover the body of a 25-year-old woman from the eighth floor of a building in Batu Maung here today.
The Bayan Baru Fire and Rescue Station received a request for assistance from police at 9.19am.
According to a post on the Bayan Baru Fire and Rescue Station's Facebook page, firefighters confirmed upon arrival that the woman's body was at the location and began efforts to safely recover it.
"Firefighters used hydraulic equipment, including a spreader, to open and lever part of the piping before lowering the body using a basket stretcher," it said.
The operation was assisted by police and a medical team from the Malaysian Red Crescent Society Penang.
The body was later handed over to police for further action.
The operation, led by Isparizan Ishak, ended at 10.39am.
The fire and rescue department advised the public against attempting technical rescue operations themselves, urging them to seek assistance from rescue agencies and authorities to ensure everyone's safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Search ongoing for missing 26-year-old Kafa teacher in Bayan Lepas
Article:
BALIK PULAU: Police have urged the public not to spread unverified information or speculate about the disappearance of a 26-year-old Kafa teacher.
Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said investigations and efforts to locate Mohamad Hijazi Zamri were ongoing.
"Police are also scrutinising information circulating about the case," he said today, warning that unverified claims could cause public concern and disrupt the investigation.
Hijazi was reported missing after leaving his home in Sungai Ara, Bayan Lepas, on Aug 22.
He had sought his mother's permission to go to Surau Al-Muttaqin in Lilitan Sungai Ara on a blue Yamaha LC135 motorcycle bearing registration number PQG 275.
However, he failed to return home and could not be reached by his family. His father lodged a
police report
on Aug 23.
Anuwal urged anyone with information on the man's whereabouts to contact the southwest district police headquarters at 04-8662222 or the nearest police station.

Title: Buying strata? New housing policy proposes showing long-term maintenance costs upfront, tighter management rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Buying a strata property could eventually involve more than knowing the purchase price, monthly instalment and maintenance fee.
With the recently launched National Housing Policy or Dasar Perumahan Negara (DRN) 2026-2035, the government proposes factoring longer-term maintenance and replacement costs into sale and purchase agreements for strata housing.
It is among several measures in the DRN aimed at improving the long-term maintenance and management of housing, including better maintenance planning, professional building management and amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757).
The policy takes a life-cycle approach to housing, meaning the focus is not only on constructing and selling a property but also on how much it will cost to operate, maintain and eventually replace components of a building over its useful life.
Firstly, what are strata and non-strata properties?
A strata property is one where ownership is divided into individual parcels or units, while areas and facilities such as lifts, corridors, swimming pools, landscaping and other shared facilities are treated as common property.
Condominiums and apartments are the most familiar examples, although certain landed developments can also be strata schemes.
Owners therefore have rights and responsibilities relating to both their individual parcel and common property, which is why they pay maintenance charges and contribute to a sinking fund.
A strata property is individually owned but shares common facilities and maintenance costs with other owners. — File picture by Hari Anggara
A non-strata property, such as a conventional landed house with its own individual title, generally does not operate under the same shared management structure.
This distinction matters because the condition of common facilities can affect the cost and value of a strata property even though they are outside the individual unit.
Maintenance and replacement costs
One of the DRN’s specific proposals is to amend sale and purchase agreements for strata housing to include estimated maintenance charges and replacement costs throughout the property’s life cycle.
The policy would give buyers a clearer picture of the longer-term cost of owning a property, beyond its purchase price and recurring maintenance charges.
Life Cycle Costing
The DRN proposes the use of Life Cycle Costing (LCC) for the design and maintenance of public housing, referring to the LCCsoft (software) application developed by the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) and the JKR Life Cycle Costing manual.
Life-cycle costing considers the total cost of an asset over its useful life, including operation, maintenance and future replacement.
The DRN also proposes guidelines for housing maintenance and facility management.
Strata management and maintenance costs
The policy proposes a performance assessment approach for strata management, including how maintenance costs are managed.
Rather than focusing only on whether maintenance fees are low, the approach would consider whether spending is adequate and sustainable given the age, design, facilities and condition of a development.
JMBs, MCs and strata management
The DRN is looking to strengthen the capacity and understanding of Joint Management Bodies (JMBs) and Management Corporations (MCs).
Under the existing framework, the Strata Management Act governs strata management, while the Strata Titles Act 1985 (Act 318) covers strata ownership.
A JMB operates during the joint-management period, while an MC comes into existence when the strata register is opened.
The government also plans to amend the Strata Management Act as part of the policy, with the changes intended to keep pace with the changing needs of strata management.
Professional management
The policy proposes increasing the number of professional building and property managers, alongside training for officials involved in property, planning and housing management.
The aim is to strengthen professional capacity in managing increasingly complex strata developments, including common facilities, maintenance, finances and insurance.
Building condition and urban renewal
The DRN requires dilapidation reports for residential buildings identified for urban renewal and building condition reports for public-housing maintenance.
Such reports could help determine whether a building requires maintenance, rehabilitation or redevelopment.
It wants to improve urban renewal guidelines, cost-benefit analyses (CBA) for redevelopment projects and greater protection and participation of existing communities.
For older strata schemes, this could provide a more structured basis for deciding whether a building should be maintained, rehabilitated or redeveloped.
Universal design
The DRN wants compliance with Universal Design Guidelines in all new housing developments.
Universal design aims to make buildings usable by a wider range of people, including older residents and persons with disabilities.
The policy complements measures such as grants to modify existing homes for senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
What this means for strata owners
For prospective buyers, the most significant proposal is the inclusion of estimated maintenance and replacement costs over the property’s life cycle in the sale and purchase agreement.
For existing owners, the focus is on stronger JMB and MC management, professionalisation and amendments to the Strata Management Act.
As for older developments, building-condition assessments, life-cycle costing and cost-benefit analyses could play a greater role in decisions on maintenance, rehabilitation or redevelopment.
The bigger picture
The DRN points towards a shift from managing strata buildings around their immediate maintenance needs to managing them according to their entire life cycle.
For strata owners, the question could eventually become not simply “how much is my maintenance fee”, but “what will it cost to maintain this building over its useful life”.

Title: MyKad printing services nationwide to face temporary disruption from tomorrow to Aug 31
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — MyKad printing services nationwide are expected to experience temporary disruption starting tomorrow (Aug 26) until Aug 31 following the transition process to the new generation MyKad.
The National Registration Department (JPN) said it was currently implementing the transition from the existing MyKad structure to the new generation identity card.
Members of the public without urgent needs have been advised to temporarily postpone replacing or exchanging their MyKad during the period.
“For first-time MyKad applications for 12-year-old children, parents or guardians are also encouraged to wait a while to enable their children to receive the new generation MyKad when production begins in the near future,” JPN said in a statement today.
The department said it appreciated the public’s patience and cooperation throughout the transition process and apologised for any inconvenience that might arise. — Bernama

Title: Jeffrey Cheah says metal fatigue possible cause of Sunway Lagoon roller coaster incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Group founder Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah has reportedly confirmed a roller coaster accident that injured 10 people occurred at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday.
The
New Straits Times
reported Cheah as saying authorities were investigating the incident, while he believed metal fatigue may have been a possible cause.
“It’s an incident that all of us regret very much. We are lucky that there were no fatalities,” Cheah was quoted as saying.
Subang Jaya district police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat previously said 22 people, comprising Malaysians and foreign tourists aged between 11 and 44, were on the ride when the incident occurred at about 9pm on Saturday.
He said those injured were taken to medical centres in the Subang Jaya district for treatment, with all reported to have sustained minor injuries.
Police said a report was lodged at 11.45am the following day and investigations are ongoing.

Title: Sunway Lagoon says cooperating with authorities after roller coaster incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Theme Parks says that it is currently working closely and fully cooperating with all relevant authorities as they conduct a thorough investigation into the incident involving an attraction at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday, which affected 10 guests.
Confirming the incident, the company also expressed deep regret, saying that their thoughts are with the guests and their families.
“The safety and well-being of our guests are our highest priority. Since the incident, our immediate focus has been on the care, medical needs and well-being of those affected.
“We have provided the necessary medical assistance and support, and remain in close contact with the guests and their families,” the company said in a statement today.
Sunway Theme Parks said it would also continue to provide its full assistance to the authorities and support to those who were affected.
“Sunway Theme Parks takes this matter extremely seriously. We remain firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety across our attractions and facilities,” it added.
Yesterday, Subang Jaya District Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Wan Azlan Wan Mamat was reported to have said that 10 people had sustained minor injuries in a roller coaster incident at a theme park.
The incident took place at about 9pm on Saturday, and the report was lodged with the police at 11.45am on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Public toilets maintained, markets upgraded, drains improved: Housing Ministry says six initiatives surpass targets
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — Six significant initiatives implemented by the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) under Budget 2026 have exceeded their targets as of July 31, with the maintenance of public toilets in local authority (PBT) areas recording the strongest performance at 734 per cent, said Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said the achievement reflected KPKT’s ability to implement the Madani Government agenda efficiently and responsively, particularly in providing better, more comfortable and inclusive public facilities.
“This achievement demonstrates that every ringgit allocated by the Government is being translated into tangible results that directly benefit the people.
“We do not want the allocation to remain just a figure on paper. Instead, it must translate into projects that can be seen, felt and enjoyed by the people,” he said in a statement today.
He said KPKT had successfully implemented nearly 16,000 public facility projects since the Madani Government took office in 2023, in addition to receiving prestigious accolades such as the National Development Award and the Prime Minister’s Innovation Award.
He said the public toilet maintenance initiative in PBT areas, which received an allocation of RM30 million, recorded the strongest performance at 734 per cent, with 367 projects successfully implemented compared with the original target of 50 projects.
Nga said the construction of Madani stalls and upgrading of dilapidated public markets recorded an achievement rate of 170 per cent, with 102 projects implemented compared with the target of 60 projects, involving an allocation of RM60 million.
In addition, he said 304 maintenance projects for non-Muslim places of worship were implemented compared with the initial target of 200 projects, recording an achievement rate of 152 per cent through an allocation of RM50 million.
Nga said the initiative to upgrade drainage and sewerage systems recorded an achievement rate of 102.67 per cent, with 154 projects implemented compared with the target of 150 projects, involving an allocation of RM55 million.
“This measure is part of KPKT’s ongoing efforts to strengthen basic infrastructure and improve drainage capacity, particularly to reduce the risk of disruptions and flash floods in PBT areas,” he said.
Meanwhile, Nga said all 113 projects to upgrade fire stations and fire department quarters had been successfully completed, with an allocation of RM10 million.
He said 57 out of the 64 programmes under the Bomba Bersama Rakyat Programme had been implemented as of July 31, achieving an implementation rate of 89 per cent.
“KPKT is committed to ensuring that the remaining programmes are fully implemented to achieve or exceed the 100 per cent target by the end of this year.
“This is in line with efforts to strengthen ties between the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and the community, as well as increase public awareness of fire safety and prevention,” he said.
Nga said the achievement also reflected the effectiveness of cooperation among ministries, departments, agencies, local authorities, industry partners and the community in ensuring the Malaysia Madani development agenda was implemented comprehensively.
He also said KPKT would continue to strengthen its service delivery, with a focus on performance, results and impact on the people, to ensure every planned initiative was implemented efficiently and effectively. — Bernama

Title: Strong winds, heavy rain damage Kuching International Airport roof (VIDEO)
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 25 — A section of the roof at the arrival area of Kuching International Airport (KIA) was damaged by strong winds and heavy rain today afternoon.
Airport personnel were at the scene to assess the situation, while personnel from the People’s Volunteer Corps (Rela) were conducting traffic control.
The section of roofing which collapsed due to strong winds on Aug 25, 2026 at Kuching International Airport. — Photo by Shahrul Tready
